# Definitions of Each Elements of PKE

## `Header`
The `Header` is defined as follow:

```rust
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Pod, Zeroable)]
pub struct Header {
    pub magic: u32,
    pub version_current: u32,
    pub version_minimal: u32,
    _pad1: [u8; 4],
    pub min: [u16; 3],
    _pad2: [u8; 2],
    pub max: [u16; 3],
    _pad3: [u8; 2],
    pub mode: ExecMode,
    _pad4: [u8; 3],
    pub sections: u16,
    pub entry_sec: u16,
    pub entry_off: u32,
    pub author: [u8; 32],
    pub name: [u8; 32],
    pub _reserved: [u8; 20],
}
```

Each field's descriptions:

| Field name 	| Type 	| Is public 	| Description 	|
|:---	|:---	|:---	|:---	|
| `magic` 	| `u32` 	| yes 	| The magic number of PKE. Fixed to `PKEX`. 	|
| `version_current` 	| `u32` 	| yes 	| Current PKE version. 	|
| `version_minimal` 	| `u32` 	| yes 	| The minimal version of PKE parser supported. 	|
| `_pad1` 	| `[u8; 4]` 	| no 	| Padding field #1. 	|
| `min` 	| `[u16; 3]` 	| yes 	| Minimal **kernel** version supported. The format of version is `[major, minor, patch]`. 	|
| `_pad2` 	| `[u8; 2]` 	| no 	| Padding field #2. 	|
| `max` 	| `[u16; 3]` 	| yes 	| Maximum **kernel** version supported. Formatted as above. 	|
| `_pad3` 	| `[u8; 2]` 	| no 	| Padding field #3. 	|
| `mode` 	| `ExecMode` 	| yes 	| Executable Mode. Further information see `ExecMode` type. 	|
| `_pad4` 	| `[u8; 3]` 	| no 	| Padding field #4. 	|
| `sections` 	| `u16` 	| yes 	| Section amounts of this PKE. 	|
| `entry_sec` 	| `u16` 	| yes 	| The section index where the **entry point** lives in. 	|
| `entry_off` 	| `u32` 	| yes 	| Offset bytes of this **entry point** sections. 	|
| `author` 	| `[u8; 32]` 	| yes 	| Author name. Limited to 32-bytes long, NUL byte (`\0`) not needed. 	|
| `name` 	| `[u8; 32]` 	| yes 	| App name. Limited to 32-bytes long, NUL byte (`\0`) not needed. 	|
| `reserved` 	| `[u8; 20]` 	| yes 	| Reserved fields for further features. 	|

::: {.callout-note}
According to the source code above, there are 2 derived traits that is **NOT** from Rust `std` or `core` crate, which are called `Pod` and `Zeroable`. These traits are from `bytemucks` crate, which mainly helps us check whether this struct can be directly transformed from raw data. Same sense ahead.
:::
